name: Pontius the Deacon
knownFor: Deacon of Cyprian of Carthage, who shared his exile and wrote the Life and Passion of Cyprian.
dates: Shared Cyprian's exile; Cyprian died in 258

keyWorks.title: The Life and Passion of Cyprian
keyWorks.about: Cyprian's conversion, his care in the plague, his exile and his death

remembered: Jerome of Strido calls the Life "a notable volume."

uncertain: The Life does not name its author. Jerome is the witness that Pontius wrote it, and Wilhelm Hartel's Latin edition calls it commonly attributed to him.
Pontius writes as an admirer, and passes over Cyprian's life before his conversion.

Arthur Cleveland Coxe, in a note to the American edition, says Pontius is said to have died a martyr. Ernest Cushing Richardson, in a note to his translation of Jerome, gives his death as about 260. Neither gives a source.
Pontius says Cyprian sold his gardens for the poor. Otto Ritschl thought they were confiscated later and that Pontius mistook this for a sale. Archbishop Benson rejects that view and follows Pontius.

ownWords.title: The Life and Passion of Cyprian (tr. Ernest Wallis)
